what.text: This page follows refugees from Sudan in all host countries combined.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 2820737 refugees from Sudan, the highest figure in its records for this group.
Chad hosts the largest share, 47.2%, followed by South Sudan.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Sudan in most years since 1983, most recently from 2020 to 2025, with the RSF, SLM/A, SPLM/A-North and SFA among the government's opponents.
An earlier armed conflict over Southern Sudan territory, with the SSLM, is recorded from 1963 to 1972.

when.text: UNHCR's series starts in 1963 at 13000 and reaches its highest point, 2820737, in 2025.
The sharpest recent change came between 2022 and 2023, in the same years as the latest conflict over the government.

how.text: These are year-end totals of refugees; asylum seekers from Sudan are counted in a separate series.
The sources don't say which routes people took to reach Chad, South Sudan or other countries.
